Carbon Offsets：Goodor Bad？
In recent years, climate change has become a growing problem for people
everywhere on the planet.
Scientists are searching for new ways to protect
the environment.
In fact, innovations, like electric
cars,
or wind and solar
power, are improving every day.
However, even with better technology, other
kinds of solutions are needed.
One such solution is called carbon offset.
Carbon
offsets
are
actions that indirectlv helD reduce the amount of
carbon dioxide (CO2) in the air.
People or companies can pay for these actions
to balance out the CO2 they produce.
There are various projects, from
growing plants to giving money for the development of more eco-friendly
technologies.
For example, a company which makes smartphones can pay to
plant trees.
First, they figure out how much CO2 they create when they make
smartphones.
Then, they pay
to plant enough trees to remove that same
amount of CO2 from the air.
In this case, the action of paying to plant the trees
is the carbon offset.
Carbon offsets do not prevent companies from producing
CO2.
However,
it is a method that can help address climate change while we
work on new solutions.
One example of
a carbon offset program
is the Delta Blue Carbon
project in Pakistan.
This project focuses on planting a special kind of tree,
the mangrove tree.
Mangrove trees, which grow in the area between river
and sea, can take 5-lO times more carbon from the air than other types of
trees.
One factor that enables them
to do this
is their rapid growth, but
there
is another secret.
The CO2 taken from the
air in mangrove leaves
moves to the roots, and
it is trapped there within
a layer of mud.
Investing
in environmental actions that aim to enhance this kind of CO2 processing by
ocean are also called blue carbon offsets.
－④－24－

One benefit of carbon offsets
is that they give us a little more time to
develop new technologies.
For example, airplanes still use fossil fuels.
These
fuels release a lot of CO2.
In fact, the airline industry creates about 2.5% of
all of the CO2 in our air.
The world needs air travel, but we also need to do
something about its effect on climate change.
Until we create new technologies
like electric airplanes, people and airline companies can pay for carbon offsets.
Carbon offsets can also benefit poor regions of the world at risk of being
affected by climate change. One study has shown that about 90% of the world's
poorest places depend on the forests for their needs.
Carbon offset programs
can benefit these places when they protect the land and create jobs for local
people.
One environmental project in Africa is protecting over l,500 square
kilometers of forest.
At the same time, it is providing jobs for over l30 people.
While carbon offsets can be helpful, they also have some disadvantages.
One problem
is that the rules concerning carbon offsets are different in
different countries and regions.
The most popular market for carbon offsets is
in the European Union・Other markets in parts of Asia and the United States
are growing. Some of these places have stricter rules than others.
This makes
it difficult to understand the value of different carbon offset programs.
Another problem with carbon offsets is "greenwashing."
Greenwashing
is the practice of companies pretending to care about the environment.
For
example, 0ne large oil company set up a carbon offset program in China.
The
company said they would teach farmers how to reduce greenhouse gasses
when growing rice.
However, in reality, many of the farmers already grew rice
this way.
The
oil company's carbon offset program turned out to make little
difference.
Thus, greenwashing could trick people into believing a company is
green. The real goal, however, should be to protect the environment.
Lack of harmony between a carbon offSet project and the local community
is reported in Peru.
In this project, the local government suddenly designated
some particular areas in the rainforest as protected areas, and forced the local
residents there to move to other places.
Some residents unexpectedly lost
their farms or jobs, and not everyone thinks this is fair.
What we have to remember is that carbon offsets are just one solution to
－④－25－

the current situation.
Some researchers argue that in reality they cancel out
only a small amount of the CO2 in the air.
To have a better chance at slowing
climate change, companies also need to use clean energy, protect forests and
oceans, and create less waste.
Only with bigger changes can we make the
world healthv and safe for the future.
－④－26－
